text:
liam: FYI after yesterday's RBAC cleanup I see unexpected outbound KMS calls from priv-cluster to 18.197.45.11. Not sure if it's a misroute or leaked token. Anyone around?

ops-bot: [ANOMALY] egress pattern anomaly for cluster priv-cluster detected at 2026-03-22T19:10Z. 63 connections to 18.197.45.11 from serviceAccount:secrets-handler. Flagging for triage.

anita: Oncall here. Can you post the kubectl patch you applied and the workload labels? Need to check rolebindings, ClusterRoleBindings, and any impersonation events.

liam: Patch was a rolebinding reduction for ns=infra to disallow secret creation. Ran at 19:08:40UTC. Cmd: `kubectl patch rolebinding infra-secrets -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/roleRef/name","value":"infra-read"}]'`.

dinesh: Pulling VPC flow logs now. NAT gateway shows outbound at 19:09:12. Which pod had spikes? run `kubectl top pod -n infra --containers`.

clare: Suggest containment: rotate serviceAccount token, cordon+drain the node if multiple pods affected, and remove egress access at the network level if target looks external. I'll prepare a short rollback for the RBAC change.

jen: I'll create an ephemeral service account and patch the Deployment to use it while we investigate. Commands I'll run:
```
kubectl create sa temp-noegress -n infra
kubectl patch deploy secrets-watcher -n infra -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"temp-noegress"}}}}'
```

maria: Also collect audit logs (kube-apiserver, kubelet, and our audit-proxy). Check for `impersonate` or token exchange events and any anomalous `decrypt` requests to KMS. I'll open a vuln-triage ticket and contact compliance if keys were accessed externally.

liam: pasted kube-audit snippet showing GET /v1/decrypt from serviceaccount:secrets-handler at 19:09:13. No impersonate entries nearby.

security-bot: [INFO] KMS policy lookup: 18.197.45.11 resolves to kms-legacy.example.net (external). Recommend immediate deny in egress ACLs if not expected.

anita: If it's external, that's a policy violation. Steps: 1) revoke any long-lived tokens for that SA 2) rotate KMS key grants to remove that host 3) run `skopeo`/`trivy` scan on the image for possible baked-in creds 4) preserve node and pod filesystem for forensic imaging.

dinesh: I've snapshot the pod's /var/run/secrets and exported token usage counts. No signs of other SAs using the token. Could be the app retried cached requests after role change. Let's rotate tokens and redeploy quickly.

clare: I'll update the RBAC rollback playbook with a step to run service-account last-used check and to gate RBAC changes with a smoke egress probe. We'll add a post-change telemetry assertion to detect outbound KMS hits within 5 minutes.

liam: containment done: replaced SA on the deployment, restarted pods, and applied egress deny for 18.197.45.11 at the VPC level. Monitoring for repeats.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-349  Priv-deploy egress KMS access. Assignees: anita, dinesh, jen. Priority: P2.

maria: I'll own the vuln-triage and log collection. Notifying product security and legal for possible data export.

jen: For evidence I uploaded the kube-audit lines and a tarball of pod env to the incident ticket.

anita: After action items: 1) add RBAC change preflight e2e with egress probe 2) require brief maintenance window for RBAC patches that affect secrets-creating roles 3) add automated alert on KMS-host hits from private clusters 4) review long-lived SA tokens and adopt projected short TTLs.

liam: Thanks all. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem once we have root cause.
